top_blockers.pattern: promql metric or label name cannot be an NRQL attribute name (a character NRQL rejects)
smart detector alert rule: Azure runs a machine-learning detector that New Relic does not have: detector VMMemoryLeak
kql table comes from an agent or service that New Relic does not read: Heartbeat has no filter that tells its rows apart from other logs, so the count would include every log line
dynamic threshold: not converted to a New Relic baseline condition; only a metric alert with a readable sensitivity, operator and failing periods is
metric alert has no readable criteria
metric name cannot be written as a New Relic name: \Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time
scope lists several resource groups or subscriptions: one New Relic condition matches one resource id prefix
window is longer than the six hours New Relic accepts for an aggregation window
availability test alert: Azure counts failing test locations, which has no mapping
metric name cannot be written as a New Relic name: CustomMetric_\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time
alarm actions (such as SNS topics) must be configured manually
composite alarm combines {N} alarms ({LIST}); New Relic has no composite condition. Recreate as one NRQL condition or filter in a workflow
metric math uses syntax that is not supported yet
period {N}s (high-resolution) is not supported
metric or dimension name has characters that are not supported

anomaly monitor: Datadog compares each point with a learned band ({LIST}) and fires when a fraction of the alert window is outside it; New Relic baseline conditions use a different model and a different trigger rule. A disabled baseline condition carrying these parameters is planned for milestone D5

change alert: Datadog compares the value with the value an interval earlier (change or pct_change); a New Relic condition cannot compare two windows and NRQL COMPARE WITH is not allowed in conditions. No automatic conversion is planned; use a baseline condition or a fixed threshold
multi-query formula monitor: the formula refers to named sub-queries in options.variables (or formula() in the query); a New Relic condition holds one query. Planned for milestone D5
query function: as_rate() divides by the sampling interval; rate() inside a New Relic condition is UNVERIFIED. Planned for milestone D5
window is longer than the six hours New Relic accepts for an aggregation window

service check monitor: counts statuses ({LIST}) of a check that an agent reports; that data exists in New Relic only if the check is re-ingested. Decide whether a host-not-reporting condition, a synthetic monitor or an NRQL condition on re-ingested results replaces it
cumulative window: the current_* window grows from a calendar boundary and resets; a New Relic condition has only rolling windows, so there is no equivalent
query function: abs() is not converted (arithmetic functions are not planned; write the expression in NRQL by hand)

forecast monitor: Datadog alerts when a linear or seasonal forecast is predicted to cross the threshold; New Relic has predictive thresholds (predict_by) with a different model. Planned for milestone D5
message contains {N} @handles: destinations are not created from them (milestone D4); each one must be configured by hand and the handle names are not carried into the output
MQL conditions are not converted
a metric-absence condition has no automatic conversion
